title: OpenCode Review: Because I Hit Claude Code Usage Limits (Claude Code vs OpenCode vs Codex CLI)
summary: Developer tries OpenCode with an OpenAI subscription after hitting Claude Code limits; compares harness features.

assertions.quote: after only like 30 minutes with Opus 4.5, I didn't have any usage left

verdicts.note: Rate-limit and cost complaints about Claude Code are common and real for heavy users, but competitors also cap usage; anecdotal, from a competitor's video.

assertions.quote: Anthropic basically blocking the usage of your Claude Code subscription with external services ... OpenAI ... fully allow you

verdicts.note: In early 2026 Anthropic blocked consumer-plan OAuth in third-party agents like OpenCode, and OpenAI announced official ChatGPT-login support there.

assertions.quote: plan mode, LSPs, the Vim mode, the sub agents ... simply aren't included in the intentionally very simple CLI tool of Codex

verdicts.note: True of features at the time (LSP, agents, plan mode); Codex CLI has since added several, and 'richer' isn't 'better results'.

assertions.quote: the model really isn't trained for the tools that open code provides

verdicts.note: Models are tuned on their vendors' harnesses and often score higher there, but third-party harnesses sometimes match or beat them on benchmarks (e.g. Terminal-Bench).

assertions.quote: Claude uses a different format ... you will have to rename that to agents.markdown

verdicts.note: AGENTS.md vs CLAUDE.md vs .cursor/rules and different skill folders are documented differences; standardization is ongoing.
